messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Service /v1/generate 5xx increase detected in canary pool (region: us-west). Error rate 6% over 2m, latency spike. Auto-escalation to on-call.

alice: seeing customer errors in Sentry too. Is this the recent canary cutover?

dan: yes, cutover started ~1709999900. Checking canary logs now.

carla: quick glance: multiple canary pods are OOMKilled (SIGKILL) right after startup. ReplicaSet scaled to 6, but 3 crashlooping.

frank: oh no — any hints in kubelet?

carla: tail of pod logs: 
```
2024-02-10T18:13:10Z ERROR OutOfMemory: allocation failed
2024-02-10T18:13:11Z INFO process received SIGKILL
```
`kubectl describe pod` shows eviction due to memory pressure and node-problem-not-ready for two nodes.

dan: HPA config for canary looks wrong — minReplicas=5, targetCPU=10%, targetMemory not set. When pods spike memory at init they all get scheduled and node OOMs. I think HPA aggressively scaled before readiness probes passed.

alice: customer impact? any regions affected beyond that canary pool?

frank: datapoint from infra metrics: request error rate jump confined to canary region traffic split (10% routed). About 0.9% of total production requests failed in past 8m, mostly 502/503. No billing impact yet but user-facing errors.

incident-bot: Paging on-call: @sre-oncall — please join.

sre-oncall: on it. Recommending immediate mitigation: 1) flip feature flag to divert canary traffic back to stable, 2) scale down canary ReplicaSet to 0, 3) rollback canary image to previous tag if flip insufficient.

alice: can we flip the FF now? Which flag?

frank: flag is `release_2024_02_canary`. I'm toggling to `off` now.

frank: toggled `release_2024_02_canary: off` -> traffic routing rule updated, starting to converge. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Deployed routing change: traffic split updated from 10%->0% for canary (id: route-983). Propagation ETA ~30s.

carla: in parallel I'm scaling the canary RS to 0 to stop further pod churn: `kubectl scale rs canary-2024-02 --replicas=0` -> success.

dan: rolling cluster note: two nodes reported kernel OOM events; I'm cordoning the nodes to avoid new pods landing while we triage: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-23-45` & `ip-10-0-23-46`.

carla: good. Will drain later after we confirm stable. For now keep them cordoned.

alice: any need to rollback stable image? or FF was sufficient?

frank: traffic is back to stable; error rate dropping to baseline within 2m. I'm still going to roll back canary RS image to previous tag in case of manual re-run: `image: inference:v1.43 -> inference:v1.42`. I'll hold that behind an explicit deploy.

sre-oncall: recommend follow-up: update HPA to include memory target or set safer minReplicas for canary (2), add readiness gate to prevent aggressive scaling, and add init memory cap in the pod spec.

dan: filing a quick postmortem ticket and labeling as SEV-2 (no major customer outage but user impact).

carla: adding logs and `kubectl describe` snippets to ticket. Also recording the nodes' kernel logs for OOM investigation.

alice: Customer comms? small spike, most traffic unaffected, but some API consumers saw 5xx for ~7m. We should prepare a brief note: what happened, mitigation (FF toggle + scale down), and next steps.

frank: I'll draft the message and drop in #announcements for approval.

incident-bot: Incident team: alice (PM), dan (eng), carla (SRE), frank (deploy) — handoff complete.

sre-oncall: Follow-up owners: carla for cluster/HPA changes, dan for manifest/CI change to prevent future auto-scale before readiness, frank for rollout/runbook updates. Estimate 2 days to complete mitigations.

alice: thanks everyone. Marking thread: resolved -> monitoring. :eyes:

frank: closing canary RS logs and archiving crash artifacts to s3://redwood-incidents/1709999999/ for the postmortem.

carla: final check: nodes cordoned, traffic stable, error rate back to baseline. I'll uncordon nodes after we patch kernel knobs and confirm memory caps.

alice: last status?

frank: final: service error rate normal, canary pool scaled to 0, routing reverted. Moving to follow-up.

alice: thanks all.
